Subject: Handling of Sensitive Financial Information in Board Minutes
From: emily.baron@wework.com
To: james.williams@wework.com, sarah.chen@wework.com, david.kim@wework.com
Date: 2026-10-16 14:23:18

James,

Following yesterday's difficult discussion, I've been advised by our litigation counsel that the creditors' lawsuit makes discovery of board minutes likely. Given the serious nature of the financial disclosures made (particularly regarding covenant violations and potential default), I recommend we maintain two sets of records:

1. Internal working notes (which can remain detailed)
2. Official minutes for corporate filing (which should be high-level)

The official minutes should focus on governance matters and avoid specific financial warnings, default scenarios, or restructuring discussions that could be used against us in litigation. We can note that financial performance was reviewed and that management is developing plans to address challenges, but should avoid specifics.

This approach is consistent with how other companies in our position have handled similar situations. The detailed analysis can remain in our internal working documents and financial models.

Best,
Emily
